You can easily export and import your LegendKeeper projects.
LegendKeeper is a powerful, specialized tool, but we never want you to feel like your content is locked up.
You can export your written content to Markdown and HTML, and you can export all of your worldbuilding content as JSON or LK files.
We also offer a variety of import options for easily bringing data into LK.
Work offline and sync up later using LegendKeeper's offline support.

LegendKeeper is a web application you can access from your browser, but you can also use it offline. When you go offline, LegendKeeper holds on to your changes, and will sync them with the server when you go back online.
If you'd like a more app-like experience with LegendKeeper, you can also use it as a "Progressive Web App" if your browser supports it.
For example, in Chrome you can click the "Install" button in your address bar to save LegendKeeper as an app to your desktop.

Every LegendKeeper project is made up of
pages
. Pages can be accessed and created from the Project Browser on the left.

A page can represent anything, including a person, place, thing, event, a piece of lore, a chapter of a book, etc. They can contain any number of wiki page, map, or whiteboard tabs. Drag and drop pages and tabs to reorder them and nest them under each other.
Here are some things you can do to quickly learn the basics.
Create a new project
Congrats! You made a new LegendKeeper project!
Type
in the editor to open the command menu
This lets you format your text and create useful content blocks.
Create a new tab
Click the 'Add Tab' button that appears when you hover this page's title. From here, you can add a new content tab.
Create a new page
Click the Create button at the bottom of the left sidebar to create a new page at the top level.
Type
to link to other pages

This helps you quickly create a connected world. You can even create new pages from the @-mention menu. If a page has multiple tabs, type a colon (:) after a mention to specify what tab you'd like to link to.
Find the extended options for pages

Press the Element Menu button with three dots in the top right corner. Here you can add tabs, adjust page layout, magically link pages with Auto-link, toggle pin clustering options for maps, and more.
Upload your first map
Add a map tab to this page by pressing the 'Add Tab' button that appears when you hover the title. Click 'Map' on the blank tab screen, 'Add map image', and then select an image to use as a map.
Add your first map pin
Right click on a map and select 'Create page', 'Link page', or drag a page from the Project Browser onto your map.
Use a template

Create a new page using the create button in the bottom left, and then select a template from the template selector. Any page you drag into the Templates tab in your Project Browser becomes a re-usable template.

content.text: Organize major events, conflicts, and discoveries with rich visual storytelling—from the arrival of legendary figures to epic wars that shaped your realm.

With Timelines, you can build a rich, immersive history for your project. Events are backed by real calendar math for dynamic calculations and displaying events to scale. Events can stand alone, or be linked to your other lore pages.
Here's what you can do starting today:
Visualize complex campaign timelines with LegendKeeper's Gantt chart view—track overlapping adventures, wars, and events across your custom fantasy calendar.
Three powerful views
List view for the big chronological picture,
Gantt view for exploring and comparing events at scale,
classic Calendar view for the daily details.
Plan your campaign with LegendKeeper's calendar view—track party arrivals, festivals, conflicts, and world events across your custom timeline.
Style controls
; make your timeline sexy with custom colors and images.
Drag and drop
for easy event editing.
Custom calendars
14 months? 28-hour days? Tamriel-inspired time system? Just do it, bay-beeee.
Choose from popular fantasy calendars or create your own—LegendKeeper supports Harptos, Exandria, Elder Scrolls, and custom systems.
Connect everything  -
Link events to your maps, lore pages, and characters.
Groups -
Group and filter your events by topic to keep things clear and organized.
Multiple timelines -
Keep separate histories (with separate calendars even) for different worlds, characters, or storylines, and then merge them together in a linked & synced master timeline.
Detail levels -
we probably don't need to know that the Endless Age of Shadows started on 1300 Floobsday the 5th at 8:36pm; use dynamic detail levels to only show the relevant bits.

LegendKeeper's interactive maps let you bring your world to life with pins, regions, paths, labels, and more.
Upload any image to use as a map. LegendKeeper handles images of any size, automatically processing them for smooth panning and zooming.
The Map Toolbar
The toolbar at the bottom of the map gives you access to all the drawing and editing tools. Select a tool to start creating map objects.
Pins
Pins are markers you place on your map to represent locations, characters, or points of interest. Each pin can be linked to a resource in your project.
Right-click
anywhere on the map to create a pin
Drag
a resource from the sidebar onto the map to create a linked pin
Customize pin icons with different shapes, colors, and glyphs
Double-click
a pin to navigate to its linked resource
Enable clustering to group nearby pins when zoomed out
Labels
Add standalone text labels to annotate your maps. Labels support custom fonts, sizes, colors, and styling options.
Regions
Draw regions to highlight areas on your map like territories, districts, or zones of influence. Regions support multiple drawing modes:
Polygon
- Click to place vertices, creating precise shapes
Rectangle
- Click and drag to create rectangular regions
Circle
- Click and drag to create circular regions
Freehand
- Draw freely to create organic shapes
Customize regions with fill colors, patterns, stroke styles, and opacity. You can also edit vertices after creation by selecting a region and dragging its control points.
Paths
Create paths to represent roads, rivers, trade routes, or any linear feature. Paths can be drawn as polylines or freehand curves.
Polyline
- Click to place points, creating smooth spline curves
Freehand
- Draw continuously for natural-looking paths
Add labels to paths and customize their stroke style, color, and width.
Measurement
Use the measurement tool to calculate distances and areas on your map. Once you've calibrated your map, measurements display in your chosen units (feet, meters, miles, etc.).
Navigation & Pathfinding
LegendKeeper can calculate routes between locations using the paths you've drawn on your map. Set waypoints and get directions with landmarks along the way.
Zoom Visibility

Control when map objects appear based on zoom level. Use the visibility range slider to set which zoom levels show each object. This helps keep your maps clean at different scales - show countries when zoomed out, cities at medium zoom, and individual buildings when zoomed in.
Organizing with Folders
Keep your map objects organized using folders. Group related pins, regions, and paths together, and toggle visibility for entire folders at once.
Selection & Editing

Select objects by clicking them, or drag a marquee to select multiple objects at once. Selected objects can be moved, styled, or deleted together. The selection sidebar shows properties for the selected object(s), letting you edit colors, styles, links, and more.
Real-time Collaboration
Work on maps together in real-time. See your collaborators' cursors as they move around the map, and watch changes appear instantly as they're made.
